questions.stem: Why do solid ionic compounds not conduct electricity?

options.text: They have no electrons at all
The ions are fixed in position and cannot move to carry charge
The ionic bonds are too weak to allow current to flow

questions.explanation: In solid ionic compounds, the ions are held in fixed positions within the giant ionic lattice. Because the ions cannot move, they cannot carry electrical charge. When melted or dissolved, the ions become free to move and can then conduct electricity.

questions.stem: Why does magnesium oxide have a higher melting point than sodium chloride?

options.text: Magnesium oxide has more atoms in its formula
Magnesium oxide has a larger lattice structure
Mg2+ and O2- have higher charges, creating stronger electrostatic attractions
Magnesium oxide contains covalent bonds as well as ionic bonds

questions.explanation: Magnesium oxide contains Mg2+ and O2- ions, which have higher charges than the Na+ and Cl- ions in sodium chloride. Higher charges produce stronger electrostatic attractions between the ions, so more energy is needed to overcome these forces.
